clue.text: Migratory cod aim north, up the creek

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

indicators.note: being up the creek means in a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fish wandering north finds itself in trouble upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the creek' means in a mess, so it scrambles the fish and the aim; north's letter leads the answer even though the clue gives it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples who move with the seasons are migratory in the same way.

clue.text: Once again supporting plants the others like to force

parts.note: the rest means the others
akin means like or similar
g is the symbol for the force of gravity, as in g-force

explanation.surface: A gardener putting fresh canes in while everyone else tries to force the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden plants are held up by stakes, so giving them new stakes is supporting them again.

clue.text: Lower bachelors into the river

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales, the crossword's favourite river
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, so bachelors are BAS

explanation.surface: Graduates being lowered into a river, perhaps as a student prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade something is to lower its quality or standing.

clue.text: Sailors in the drink

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, so sailors are ABS

explanation.surface: Seamen who have had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the drink' is slang for fallen into the sea, which suits sailors, but the drink is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Enacted to give a nicer flat to a MP?

indicators.note: the listed words are made to give something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Legislation passed so that an MP gets a nicer flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' rearranges the words after the first A into the rest of the answer; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by the legislature is what has been enacted into law.

clue.text: Brush his smirk off!

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: An order to wipe the smug look off someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges HIS SMIRK into the answer; 'Brush' is a noun here, a brief clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush with the enemy is a short fight, a minor clash.

clue.text: Barely visible

parts.note: read as 'visible in the bare', i.e. seen with no clothes on, rather than faintly seen

explanation.definitionFit: Someone unclothed is on view in the bare skin.

clue.text: With this cooked Indian meal he gets a Coke free

indicators.note: free means the letters are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who gets a free cola with his Indian dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges HE, A and COKE. Indian meal is cornmeal, not a curry: the definition describes a cake cooked with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoecake is a simple American flatbread baked from cornmeal, once called Indian meal.

clue.text: Stick togther with the man in charge present

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, the man in charge
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Staying loyal when the boss is in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold together firmly is to stick or bind as a unit.

clue.text: More difficult to stack in a row

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: Stacking things in a line is the harder task.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trickier needs more skill, so it is harder.

clue.text: Against tucking into pudding, at the foot of the Andes

definitions.text: at the foot of the Andes

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sago is a milk pudding
anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to eat their dessert while in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, which fits the pudding, but here it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chilean capital lies in a valley below the Andes range.

clue.text: Rotten to eat? Just so

parts.note: a fruit that is indeed eaten only once it has gone soft and half-rotten

explanation.definitionFit: This small brown fruit is left to blet, decaying until soft, before eating.

clue.text: Hitch-hiker's request for a tonic

definitions.meaning: a person thumbing a lift asks drivers to stop and take them
a restorative drink or anything that lifts the spirits

explanation.definitionFit: A restorative drink is so called because it raises one's spirits, the same words a hitcher would say.

clue.text: Was responsible when weeds ran riot

indicators.note: running riot means going wild, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A gardener taking the blame when the weeds took over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran riot' reads as one phrase, but RAN is fodder and 'riot' alone rearranges WEEDS RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: One who answered for something was accountable for it.

clue.text: Pepsi-cola cocktail is for the bishop

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A soft-drink mixture prepared for the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcopal matter is one concerning or belonging to bishops.

clue.text: Begging for breakfast in a doorway

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an entry is a doorway or entrance
to breakfast is to eat

explanation.surface: A homeless person asking for breakfast in a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest plea or request is an act of begging.

clue.text: An oil-rig abandoned —— it was first in the field

definitions.text: it was first in the field

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deserted drilling platform that was the first in its oilfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Something first of its kind, preceding all others, is the prototype in its field.

clue.text: On the right hand, there's hatred from a hard element

parts.note: odium means hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: Resentment emerging from a hard person on someone's right.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard silvery metal is a chemical element of the platinum group.

clue.text: At English resort, suffering from sunburn and hung over

parts.note: Hove is a seaside resort in Sussex, next to Brighton
sunburnt skin is red

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker at the seaside, burnt and nursing a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hovered stayed suspended in the air above a place.

clue.text: Cheat tax on gold

parts.note: an impost is a tax or duty
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Dodging the duty on gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' could signal order, but here it is part of the leaf for gold; the charade order is natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud passing as someone else is a cheat.

clue.text: Foot the bill or ask for a little more rope?

definitions.meaning: to cover the cost of something

definitions.text: ask for a little more rope
definitions.meaning: a climber's call to let out more line

explanation.definitionFit: Paying money and letting a rope run out are both expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Land reclaimed from a Prince earlier

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
older means from an earlier time

explanation.surface: Territory taken back from a former prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch low-lying land won back from the sea is reclaimed land.

clue.text: Meaning to go with the tide

definitions.meaning: the gist or sense of what is said
to be carried along by the current

explanation.definitionFit: The general sense of a speech and floating with the current share one word.

clue.text: Dressed for the annual dance, but likely to slope off

parts.note: may expresses likelihood, as in 'it may rain'

indicators.note: off shows the letters are moved out of their order

explanation.surface: Dancers dressed up for the yearly ball who are likely to sneak off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SLOPE into POLES. Dressed means decorated with ribbons and garlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall posts decorated with ribbons for May Day dancing are dressed for the spring festival.

clue.text: Foolish girl we hear calling for mineral in glass

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a silly Kate, a foolish girl named Kate

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for a daft girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' gives the sound of SILLY KATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon-oxygen compounds form most rocks and are the main ingredient of glass.

clue.text: Bold girl tied the knot

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
to tie the knot is to marry

explanation.surface: A brave young woman who got married.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not overawed is fearless and bold.

clue.text: A stone makes them stay

indicators.note: makes signals that the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: A heavy stone that forces people to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges THEM STAY into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple quartz is a semi-precious gemstone.
